slides.title: 5 Thanksgiving turkey myths that could ruin dinner

slides.myth: It's fine to thaw the turkey on the counter overnight.
slides.fact: Never on the counter. Thaw it in the fridge, about 24 hours for every 4 to 5 pounds, or in cold water you change every 30 minutes.
slides.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

slides.myth: Forgot to thaw it? You can't cook a frozen turkey.
slides.fact: You can, and it's safe. It just takes at least 50% longer than a thawed bird, so start early and check it with a thermometer.
slides.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

slides.myth: When the pop-up timer pops, the turkey is done.
slides.fact: USDA still says use a food thermometer: 165°F in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost part of the thigh and wing.

slides.myth: If the meat is still a little pink, it's undercooked.
slides.fact: Color isn't the test. Turkey that reached 165°F everywhere is safe to eat, even if some of the meat stays pink.

slides.myth: If the turkey is done, the stuffing inside is done too.
slides.fact: The center of the stuffing needs to hit 165°F on its own. USDA says the safest way is to bake it in a separate dish.
slides.source: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
